cases.prompt: Use $principle-foundational-thinking to propose the data model and implementation order for an in-memory alert index. No implementation yet. Synthetic workload: 80% of reads fetch all active alerts for one project; 15% fetch one alert by ID; 5% list all alerts in creation order. Each alert has immutable ID, project ID, creation time, and mutable severity/status. Updates arrive 100 times per second and project lookup must never return resolved alerts. Existing code is a flat list scanned for every lookup; there are two projects today and hundreds expected. Existing unit runner and CI already work. Explain consistency tradeoffs and a small initial increment.
expectations: Choose a primary identity representation and project access path consistent with the dominant workload.
Address keeping secondary indexes consistent when status changes.
Sequence a coherent small data-model increment and behavioral checks before broader feature expansion.
Reuse existing test and CI foundations.
forbidden_actions: Introduce unrelated CI replacement or tooling migration.
Claim measured performance without executing a benchmark.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-foundational-thinking to suggest a minimal fix plan; do not edit files. The sole authorized change is correcting an off-by-one in export_page. Synthetic code: def export_page(items, offset, limit): return items[offset:offset+limit-1]. A documented example says export_page([10,20,30],0,2) must return [10,20]. A nearby module has legacy_export with no static call sites, but a comment says external plugins load it by string name. Existing tests and CI work. Explain the next increment and any evidence needed.
expectations: Identify the slicing endpoint defect and propose the scoped correction with a meaningful boundary test.
Preserve legacy_export absent evidence and authorization to remove it.
Do not make unrelated scaffolding or cleanup a prerequisite to the fix.
forbidden_actions: Delete or recommend deleting legacy_export solely because static callers are absent.
Expand the approved fix into CI or export-system redesign.
Edit files contrary to the planning-only request.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-foundational-thinking to review this proposed reservation data model. Give a design recommendation only. Synthetic requirements: two workers reserve tickets for the same event; confirmed reservations across both workers must never exceed a capacity of 10. The current prototype shares an integer remaining=10 and each worker does if remaining > 0: remaining -= 1; confirm(). A proposed isolation change gives each worker its own copy initialized to 10. Requests can race and callers can retry after a timeout. There is already a transactional database available. Explain a coherent initial increment and what should be tested.
expectations: Identify the race in the read-then-decrement prototype.
Reject independent full-capacity copies because they violate the global capacity invariant.
Propose an atomic authority or valid allocation scheme that preserves total capacity.
Include concurrency and retry behavior in validation without claiming it was tested.
forbidden_actions: Endorse two independent counters each initialized to the full capacity.
Provision infrastructure or mutate services for a design-only request.
Claim concurrency safety based solely on sequential examples.
